AfterCardPlayed.issue: Rollup of guards G1 (LIVE) and G2 per binding rule 4. The arithmetic and the type filter are right; the DISPATCH is not -- the sim fires on_card_played once per logical play where C# fires it once per CardPlay (G1), and fires it at all after the combat has started ending (G2).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): Hook.AfterCardPlayed fires once per Replay ITERATION in C# and once per logical play in the sim, so a replayed Attack grants 1 Block instead of 2
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CardModel.cs:1904-1965 builds a fresh CardPlay inside `for (int i = 0; i < playCount; i++)` and fires Hook.AfterCardPlayed INSIDE that loop; combat.py:514 fires on_card_played ONCE after the whole play-count loop (combat.py:477-494). This is audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json gap G4, which that record labels LIVE and pins as a strict-xfail test; one verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3 -- the seam owns the machinery and this record owns Daughter of the Wind's observable. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b04.py dotw): relics=[daughter_of_the_wind] gives 1 Block from a Strike (correct); relics=[daughter_of_the_wind, throwing_axe] STILL gives 1 Block, where C# gives 2 because the Strike plays twice and each CardPlay fires the hook. Both sides ported: the relic is one of the three dolls in the Doll Room event (events/doll_room.py:15) and Throwing Axe -- which replays the first card of each combat -- is granted by the Tanx shrine (events/tanx.py). Four further ported replay sources reach the same play-count hook (the Spiral and Glam enchantments, One-Two Punch, Duplication), all enumerated by hook_dispatch G4. RULE 7: relics/throwing_axe.py, events/doll_room.py, combat.py and CardModel.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): C# yields no listeners to a combat hook dispatched after the combat has started ending; the sim has no such gate, so a LETHAL Attack still grants its 1 Block
guards.issue: MECHANISM: Hook.IterateCombatHookListeners (Hook.cs:53-63) yields nothing once IsOverOrEnding is set, and 73 of the game's 147 dispatchers go through it; combat.py flips Phase.COMBAT_OVER only inside _end_combat and no dispatcher consults the phase. This relic is the NAMED WITNESS for audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json gap G8, whose issue text cites relics/daughter_of_the_wind.py:23-33 and records the executed observation that 'a lethal Strike still grants its 1 Block from on_card_played after _all_enemies_dead() is true'. Cited and matched, not re-derived (binding rule 3): same verdict (gap) and same DORMANT label, for the reason that record gives -- the 1 Block is combat-scoped state the combat then discards. The concrete thing that would make it live is also G8's: a listener on a guarded dispatcher that mutates RUN-level state (HP, gold, deck) from AfterCardPlayed / AfterCardDrawn / AfterCardExhausted / AfterShuffle / AfterEnergySpent; the conformance exporter is the near-term risk, because a replay that records post-lethal block would not match the save. RULE 7: hook_dispatch.json and Hook.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: N1: BlockVar(1m, ValueProp.Unpowered) (DaughterOfTheWind.cs:16) passed to CreatureCmd.GainBlock (line 23) vs BLOCK = 1 with props=DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED (daughter_of_the_wind.py:21, 30-33)
guards.rationale: Two things had to line up and both do. The CONSTANT: no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 1 is the pinned non-ascension value. The PROP: DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED is exactly ValueProp.UNPOWERED (valueprops.py:42), and BlockCmd.apply (cmds.py:130-151) gates the Dexterity/Frail additive and multiplicative modifiers behind is_powered_attack, which requires MOVE and not UNPOWERED -- so the 1 Block is flat, which is what ValueProp.Unpowered means in the source. This matters: the relic fires on every Attack, so a Dexterity misclassification would compound all fight long. RULE 7: valueprops.py and cmds.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N2: `cardPlay.Card.Owner == base.Owner` (DaughterOfTheWind.cs:20) and the PlayerChoiceContext parameter (line 18)
guards.rationale: Both are the multiplayer per-player plumbing the shared contract puts out of scope: one player exists in the sim, so the owner clause is vacuous and the choice context has nothing to route. The clause the sim DOES keep, `Card.Type == CardType.Attack` (daughter_of_the_wind.py:28-29), is the only one that can vary.

guards.what: N3: Flash() and GainBlock's `fast: true` animation flag (DaughterOfTheWind.cs:22-23)
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / RefreshCounter / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.PreviewCardPileAdd are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.
